name: Northline contact centre: staffing a day of calls
description: One day (08:00-20:00, half-hours) at a broadband provider's contact centre, played call by call by an operations queue. Calls arrive at a fitted base x a day-of-week index x a time-of-day index (fitted from contact_centre/history.csv with fg_env.analysis.fit_patterns), surging after a network outage; handle times are lognormal around the average handle time in the history; callers give up after a patience calibrated to the history's abandonment, shorter during an outage. Agents on duty per half-hour are an input vector (empty: the manager's rule, 10% over the forecast workload plus two). Arms compare the manager's rule with the plan fg_env.analysis.optimise found (the cheapest where every half-hour's expected service level reaches 80% of calls answered within 20 seconds and the day's does in 90% of runs, each held with 90% confidence), an outage at 09:30, and callbacks that keep agents free for live calls. examples/contact_centre_history.py regenerates the history from the truth arm and re-estimates the model; examples/contact_centre_plan.py searches the plan (kept in contact_centre/plan.json) and, with --report, validates the model on the two held-out weeks and prints the owner report.

day.description: The day simulated: its opening time (ISO date-time; opening must stay 08:00).

history.description: Half-hourly history: calls offered, answered, abandoned and answered within 20 s, handle and wait times, agents on duty, outage.

staffing.description: Agents on duty in each of the 24 half-hours from 08:00; empty: the manager's rule.

agent_cost.description: Cost of one agent per paid hour.

shrinkage.description: Share of paid time not on the phones (breaks, training, meetings), from the workforce plan.

aht_sec.description: Average handle time in seconds: estimated from the history (answered-weighted) by examples/contact_centre_history.py.

aht_cv.description: ASSUMED: spread of handle times (sd / mean); the history holds only half-hourly averages.

patience_sec.description: Mean time a caller waits before hanging up: calibrated to the history's daily abandonment by examples/contact_centre_history.py.

outage_at.description: When a network outage starts (only matters with outage_uplift above 0).

outage_uplift.description: Extra calls at an outage's peak, as a multiple of the normal volume (0: no outage).

outage_uplift_estimate.description: Peak uplift estimated from the outage days in the history (first half-hour's calls over the fitted forecast) by examples/contact_centre_history.py; the outage arms use it.

outage_half_life.description: ASSUMED: minutes for an outage surge to halve.

outage_patience_share.description: ASSUMED: callers' patience during an outage surge, as a share of normal patience.

callbacks.description: Offer callers facing a long wait a call back.

callback_wait_sec.description: Offer a callback when the expected wait is longer than this (seconds).

callback_accept.description: ASSUMED: share of callers offered a callback who take it.

callback_reserve.description: Agents kept free for live calls: a callback is made only while more agents than this are free.

parameter_uncertainty.description: Scales the standard errors of fitted pattern parameters: 1 draws each run's parameters around their estimates, 0 uses the estimates as they are.

weekday_profile.description: Pattern 'weekday', profile: fitted by fg_env.analysis.fit_patterns from $inputs.history (joint count regression).

hours_profile.description: Pattern 'hours', profile: fitted by fg_env.analysis.fit_patterns from $inputs.history (joint count regression).

calls_scale.description: Pattern 'calls', scale: fitted by fg_env.analysis.fit_patterns from $inputs.history (joint count regression).

centre.description: The contact centre (the queue is its mechanism).

outage.description: a network outage at 09:30 with the recommended plan

callbacks.description: callbacks offered on a normal day with the recommended plan

truth.description: The centre that generated history.csv: the true parameters, used by examples/contact_centre_history.py only.

invariants.why: inputs.weekday_profile and inputs.weekday_profile_se are the demand factor of each weekday and its standard error: give both, of one length.
inputs.hours_profile and inputs.hours_profile_se are the demand factor of each half-hour and its standard error: give both, of one length.
inputs.staffing lists the agents on duty in each of the 24 half-hours from 08:00, or is empty for the manager's rule: give it 24 numbers or none.
inputs.day is the opening of the day simulated, and the half-hours of history, staffing and the demand profile start at 08:00: give it as YYYY-MM-DDT08:00.

hours.description: time of day (the 12 opening hours, one value per half-hour from 08:00)

outage.description: the surge of calls after a network outage
